title: Reseal opened sparkling wine with a two-clamp stopper: cap on the mouth, both side clamps squeezed shut under the lip
instruction: Reseal the opened sparkling wine with the stopper.
context: Waiters and bartenders reseal opened sparkling wine sold by the glass so it keeps its fizz to the next pour (O*NET 35-3031.00 Waiters and Waitresses, 35-3011.00 Bartenders; about 2.9 million US workers together, BLS OEWS May 2024). A cork will not go back in, so bars use a clamp stopper: its cap must sit square on the mouth, and both side clamps must be squeezed in until their hooks click under the bottle's lip, or the gas pressure lifts it off.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. (1) A black rubber bar mat, 150 x 150 x 4 mm, centred at x 300, y -80. (2) On it, an opened 375 ml sparkling-wine half bottle of dark green glass, 0.95 kg with what is left in it: 80 mm across, 232 mm tall, a 25 mm neck under a 31 mm crown lip 10 mm tall (the ledge under the lip is 222 mm up), gold foil torn off above the shoulder. (3) A chrome two-clamp stopper, 60 g: a 42 mm cap with a 16 mm knob on top, whose skirt reaches 8 mm down round the lip with a rubber gasket under it, and two hinged side clamps on opposite sides (to the robot's left and right), each a 16 mm wide plate with a hook at its foot and a knurled pad on its outer face; a light spring holds each open on its 18 degree stop. It sits on a 25 mm wooden stopper peg, 80 mm tall, at x 200, y -190, clamps open.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial. 0 for the rest of the trial if the bottle tips over 20 degrees or falls. Otherwise: 1.0 (success, must hold for 1 s) when the stopper's cap is seated on the bottle's mouth (within 2.5 mm of its middle, 2 mm of its top and 5 degrees of square) with both side clamps clicked shut (squeezed to within 2 degrees of shut, where their catch holds them), both grippers 30 mm or more from the stopper and nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 when it is seated with both clamps shut but a gripper is near or something still moves; 0.5 when it is seated with one clamp shut and both grippers 30 mm or more away; 0.25 when the cap was seated on the mouth at some point; else 0.
reset_notes: Pull each clamp's foot out to unclip it, lift the stopper off and stand it back on its peg with both clamps open, to the robot's left and right. Stand the bottle back in the middle of the mat.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size; the bottle is a lathed mesh with an exact (signed-distance) collider; the stopper's cap is a disc with a 12-stave skirt, its side clamps hinged plates. Each clamp's open spring and its catch are drives on its hinge: free under a light spring until squeezed to within 2 degrees of shut, then held shut. The gasket's seal and the gas pressure are not simulated; the hooks under the lip hold the cap down. All geometry is generated by code in the package.
